sections.title: Map basics
sections.description: Put a map on screen and point it somewhere.

examples.title: Display a map
examples.description: One raster layer from one spec, and a camera pointed at it. The whole map is six lines.

sections.title: Camera
sections.description: Move, fly, frame and constrain the view.

examples.title: Fly to a location
examples.description: One flight moves position, zoom, rotation and tilt together. Four separate setters would animate independently and visibly fight.

sections.title: Sources & data
sections.description: Where tiles and features come from.

examples.title: Add a GeoJSON line
examples.description: A "geojson" source re-tiles the document on the fly, so the features are styled with CartoCSS and drawn by the same renderer as a tile server's.

sections.title: Styles & layers
sections.description: CartoCSS, style projects and layer composition.

examples.title: Change a style at runtime
examples.description: A style project declares `param::` values the app sets while the map runs. A colour swaps live; a parameter used in a filter re-decodes the tiles.

examples.title: 3D terrain, hybrid
examples.description: Satellite imagery draped over an elevation mesh, with roads and summit labels above it. One DEM source drives the mesh, the hillshade and the elevation queries.

sections.title: Markers & popups
sections.description: Things an app puts on the map itself.

examples.title: Markers and popups
examples.description: addMarker takes a spec that carries the position AND the style. Tap a summit for a balloon popup; tap the map to dismiss it.

examples.title: Get the feature under a tap
examples.description: The click payload is read lazily by path, so asking for one property never parses the whole feature - and the geometry is only serialised if you want it.

sections.title: Search & routing
sections.description: Finding features and getting from A to B.

examples.title: Search the map's own tiles
examples.description: Every filter on a search request is an ordinary property. Runs async, because a search fetches and decodes every tile in range.
